solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Mere copper wire’s ultimate tool for potter (4,3)

indicatorNotes.ultimate: the ultimate letter of 'wire' is its last, E

blocks.note: a mere is a small lake or pool
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A length of copper wire at the edge of a pond turns out to be a handy tool for someone potting about.
annotation.walkthrough: A potter here is not a ceramicist but a player who pots balls on a pool table. The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pool cue is the stick a player uses to pot balls.

entries.clue: Bird rising aloft very loudly over home (6)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising turns UP upwards to read PU
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, FF sits over IN

blocks.note: ff = fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
to be in is to be at home

annotation.surface: A bird climbs high into the sky, calling noisily above its nest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the bird itself rising; the word only flips UP in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: The puffin is a stubby seabird with a colourful beak.

entries.clue: Get rigid old ship if last in jetty (6)

indicatorNotes.last in: the last letter in 'jetty' is Y

annotation.surface: An old ship tied up at the end of a jetty might stiffen and seize up.
annotation.walkthrough: SS for steamship is the common crossword abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: To ossify is to turn into bone, and so to become rigid.

entries.clue: Restricting way to scamming that’s heartless and rotten (6,3)

indicatorNotes.heartless: remove the heart, the middle letter N, from CONNING

annotation.surface: A crooked scheme is described as cold-hearted and corrupt.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a road-works phrase: 'way' is a road, restricted by laying out traffic cones.
annotation.definitionFit: Coning off a road closes or narrows it with traffic cones.

entries.clue: Errant teen I reformed as performer (11)

indicatorNotes.reformed: the letters are formed again in a new order

annotation.surface: A wayward teenager straightens out and takes to the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Errant' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'reformed' is the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: singers, comedians and magicians who put on a show for an audience are all entertainers.

entries.clue: Avoided second defender (4,4)

blocks.note: something left alone has been avoided
to second a proposal is to back it

annotation.surface: Someone dodged the job of backing up a proposal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as a noun or ordinal, but it is the verb: to second = to back.
annotation.definitionFit: In football the left back plays in the back line on the left flank, whose job is stopping attacks.

entries.clue: Many empty libraries to stock books (4)

indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters: L and S
indicatorNotes.to stock: LS holds OT as a library holds stock

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Plenty of libraries stand empty and need books on their shelves.
annotation.walkthrough: The Old Testament is the usual crossword source for 'books' (OT or NT).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal speech: 'lots of people came' says the same as 'many people came'.

entries.clue: Element on boats ignoring core of the work regulations (7,4)

indicatorNotes.core of: the core of 'the' is its middle letter H

blocks.note: a factor is an element in a situation
middle letter of 'the', dropped from YACHTS

annotation.surface: Some element aboard the boats pays no heed to the heart of the job.
annotation.walkthrough: The Factory Acts were the British laws governing conditions in factories from the nineteenth century on.
annotation.definitionFit: The Factory Acts were laws regulating work in factories.

entries.clue: Great performance getting round nuisance on foot, hazard to driver (5,6)

indicatorNotes.getting round: to get round something is to encircle it, so BLINDER wraps itself round CORN

blocks.note: to play a blinder is to give a brilliant performance
a corn is a painful patch on the foot

annotation.surface: A star turn is achieved despite a sore foot — something that could trip up a golfer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blinder' is British slang for an outstanding performance, as in 'he played a blinder'. The driver is a motorist, not a golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: A blind corner is a bend with no view of oncoming traffic, a danger for drivers.

entries.clue: Understanding son acting badly (9)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are arranged badly and must be fixed

annotation.surface: A parent is sympathetic about their son's poor performance on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' reads as a kind parent; it is the adjective meaning aware.
annotation.definitionFit: To be cognisant of something is to be aware of or understand it.

entries.clue: One that’s cold consumes tonic (6)

indicatorNotes.consumes: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so BRR swallows ACE

blocks.note: brr! is what you say when it is cold
an ace counts one in cards

annotation.surface: Someone feeling the chill knocks back a tonic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One that's cold' looks like a single phrase about a chilly person; 'one' and 'that's cold' do separate jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: A bracer is a tonic or stiff drink that braces you.

entries.clue: On and off, church is means of support (8)

blocks.note: milk gone off has turned sour

annotation.surface: Someone's attachment to the church is an on-and-off source of strength.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On and off' looks like a phrase for intermittently; the words are taken separately.
annotation.definitionFit: Something you can fall back on or draw from when in need, like savings or friends, is a resource.

entries.clue: Nosy neighbours welcoming bird-watcher in the end (7-9)

blocks.note: a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher

annotation.surface: Busybody neighbours finally make friends with a birdwatcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally'; 'in' is a link and 'the end' gives CURTAINS.
annotation.definitionFit: Curtain-twitchers peep out from behind their curtains to watch the neighbours.

entries.clue: Again experience nurses ultimately desperate for support (7)

indicatorNotes.nurses: RELIVE holds E as a nurse holds a baby

blocks.note: to relive is to experience again

annotation.surface: Nurses go through desperate times again and need support.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the hospital staff; it is a verb, holding the E.
annotation.definitionFit: To relieve someone can mean to support or help them.

entries.clue: Hosiery items for sale among fine things around front of shop (7,9)

indicatorNotes.among: STOCK goes among the other letters
indicatorNotes.around: the letters of FINE THINGS and S are turned around into a new order
indicatorNotes.front of: the front letter of 'shop' is S

blocks.note: first letter of shop, added to the anagram
a shop's stock is its items for sale

annotation.surface: A shop shows off its stockings, set out among other fine goods at the front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Items for sale' sounds like the whole of the stock on show; only the shop's stock goes inside, and 'around' is the signal to rearrange, not to wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: these are leg coverings woven in an open diamond mesh like a fishing net, one kind among tights and socks.

entries.clue: Like court proceeding barring one of stars (6)

indicatorNotes.barring: barring means except for, so AS TRIAL is taken without the I

blocks.note: a trial is a court proceeding
I = one in Roman numerals, removed

annotation.surface: A trial goes ahead without one of the celebrities involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One of stars' reads as a single celebrity; 'one' is the removed I and 'of stars' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin astrum, a star: the word describes anything belonging to the heavens, as in astral bodies.

entries.clue: Herb increased resistance within 31 days (8)

indicatorNotes.within: within means inside, so R is placed inside the month MAY

blocks.note: May is a month of 31 days

annotation.surface: A herb's resistance to pests goes up over the course of a month.
annotation.walkthrough: '31 days' could be several months; the letter count settles on MAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: its needle-like leaves are a classic kitchen seasoning, especially with roast lamb.

entries.clue: Soldiers in buff shot (8)

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan
to have a shot = to have a try

annotation.surface: Soldiers in the nude are shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In buff' suggests 'in the buff', naked; buff is an enthusiast here.
annotation.definitionFit: The infantry are soldiers who fight on foot.

entries.clue: Launched ball at ninepins we heard striking (4)

indicatorNotes.we heard: what we heard is only the sound of BOWLED

blocks.note: in skittles or ninepins you bowl a ball at the pins

annotation.surface: A bowler hurls the ball at the skittles and we hear it hit.
annotation.walkthrough: Ninepins is the old game of skittles, where a ball is bowled at nine pins. 'Striking' looks like hitting the pins; it means eye-catching.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms for eye-catching: colours or patterns that grab your attention are called both.

entries.clue: Immunise number in critical care area recently (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so NO is placed inside ICU

annotation.surface: Patients in intensive care have lately been vaccinated in large numbers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the abbreviation NO, not a figure like TEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving someone a vaccine jab to protect them against disease is inoculating them.

entries.clue: Unwelcome wrapper in garden? (8)

blocks.note: reads as litter, but means a plant that wraps itself round others and is not wanted: a weed
the question mark flags that the wrapper is a living thing growing in the beds

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed by packaging litter blown into their garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrapper' suggests packaging; bindweed wraps itself round other plants, and a weed is unwelcome by definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bindweed is a climbing weed that winds tightly around other plants.

entries.clue: See almost everyone stifled in urban neighbourhood (8)

blocks.note: ALL, everyone, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Look how nearly everybody is suffocating in a city district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is the archaic exclamation LO, not a bishop's see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the district around a particular place, where people live nearby.

entries.clue: Work with beer technology to lose current milky quality (11)

indicatorNotes.to lose: something lost is no longer there, so SCIENCE drops its I

blocks.note: I = electric current in physics, removed

annotation.surface: Beer-brewing technology is used to get rid of cloudiness in the drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as up-to-date; it is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: Opalescence is the milky, iridescent sheen of an opal.

entries.clue: Source of heat in Asian food involving new coating on noodle (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is literally to roll up within, so SUSHI wraps round N
indicatorNotes.coating on: the coating of 'noodle' is its outer letters, N and E

annotation.surface: Some Asian dish gets its heat from a fresh coating of spice on the noodles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Source of heat in Asian food' suggests chilli; 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Sunshine is the sun's light and warmth, a source of heat.

entries.clue: Explorer’s grave reportedly revealed beneath hut (6,10)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: EARNEST as heard gives the name ERNEST
indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, LET ON goes beneath SHACK

annotation.surface: An explorer's burial place is said to have been uncovered under a hut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial site; it means serious. Shackleton led Antarctic expeditions and was himself buried on South Georgia.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Ernest Shackleton was the Anglo-Irish Antarctic explorer.

entries.clue: Official in university reviewed study without subtlety (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so REF is placed inside UNI
indicatorNotes.reviewed: re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so DEN reads backwards

blocks.note: a ref is a match official
a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: A university official gives a study a crude review.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' looks like assessed; it turns DEN round.
annotation.definitionFit: Unrefined means crude, lacking subtlety.

entries.clue: Intoxicated when clutching to a poisonous beast (4,4)

indicatorNotes.clutching: to clutch is to grip tightly, so CANED holds TO A in its grasp

blocks.note: caned is British slang for very drunk or stoned

annotation.surface: A drunk grabs hold of a venomous creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caned' is British slang for heavily drunk or high.
annotation.definitionFit: The cane toad secretes a toxin from glands in its skin.

entries.clue: Hand’s flipped this switch (4)

indicatorNotes.flipped: a flipped object is turned over end to end, so PAWS reads backwards

blocks.note: paws = hands, informally; hand's read as 'hands'

annotation.surface: Someone's hand has flicked a switch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a light switch; it is the verb meaning exchange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms as verbs: exchanging seats with a friend can be called either.

entries.clue: Secure medal bagging second place in epic game (4-4)

indicatorNotes.bagging: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so GONG holds P inside
indicatorNotes.second place in: the letter in second place in 'epic' is P

blocks.note: gong is British slang for a medal

annotation.surface: Someone wins a silver medal after an epic contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second place' looks like silver; it is the second letter of 'epic'. A gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: table tennis, named for the sound of the ball bouncing off bats and table.

entries.clue: Find fault about way of speaking (4)

blocks.note: RP = Received Pronunciation, standard British accent

annotation.surface: Someone complains about the way another person talks.
annotation.walkthrough: Received Pronunciation is the standard 'BBC' accent of southern British English.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grumbling or nitpicking about small things is carping, nothing to do with the fish.

entries.clue: That woman and rest sell bananas uncovered (11)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas = crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A woman takes a break while selling bananas without wrappers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit on sale; it means crazy and scrambles the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Shelterless means without cover or protection.

entries.clue: Reported secretion from blubber layer (4)

indicatorNotes.Reported: only the sound of TEAR is used

blocks.note: a tear comes from someone blubbering, crying

annotation.surface: Scientists report a substance oozing from a layer of whale blubber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like whale fat; it is the verb, to cry noisily.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: each stacked level of a wedding cake or stadium seating is one tier.

entries.clue: Difficult extracting essence of promotional flyer for Latino singer (5,6)

indicatorNotes.extracting: TRICKY has a letter taken out
indicatorNotes.essence of: the essence of 'promotional' is its middle letter, T

blocks.note: a martin is a bird like a swallow

annotation.surface: A tricky job pulling together a promotional leaflet for a Latin pop star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like the leaflet; it is a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Ricky Martin is a Puerto Rican pop singer.

entries.clue: One connects rebellion and affair after losing female (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a noun phrase: one = a thing that connects

indicatorNotes.after losing: FLING loses F and follows COUP

blocks.note: a coup is a seizure of power
a fling is a brief affair

annotation.surface: Someone links an uprising to a love affair, after a woman drops out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One connects' is the definition: a coupling is a thing that connects, as between railway carriages.
annotation.definitionFit: A coupling is a device that connects two things.

entries.clue: Commanding turn is then turning heads (2,3,6)

indicatorNotes.turning: IS THEN turns into a new order
indicatorNotes.heads: the anagram heads, going in front of ADDLE

blocks.note: eggs addle as milk turns: both go bad

annotation.surface: A commanding figure's spin and turn catch everyone's eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning heads' reads as attracting attention; 'turning' scrambles IS THEN and 'heads' puts that result first, ahead of ADDLE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from riding: whoever sits astride the horse controls it, so the phrase means holding power.

entries.clue: Girl from Madrid gent knew should abandon outskirts (8)

indicatorNotes.should abandon outskirts: each of the three words loses its outer letters

annotation.surface: A man knew a girl from Madrid who ought to leave the suburbs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Girl from Madrid' suggests a Spanish name; 'from' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a French feminine form of Adrian, used as a first name for women.

entries.clue: Flying parasites biting us in Baltic region, once (4,7)

indicatorNotes.Flying: the letters of PARASITES fly about
indicatorNotes.biting: the anagram bites US, taking it inside

annotation.surface: Winged parasites nibble at us in a region on the Baltic long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying parasites' reads as insects like mosquitoes; 'Flying' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: East Prussia was a German province on the Baltic, divided up after 1945.

entries.clue: Says no more and quiet operation ceases trading (5,2,4)

annotation.surface: A business goes silent and quietly stops trading.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quiet operation' reads as a discreet business; the words are SH and OP taken separately.
annotation.definitionFit: To shut up shop is to close a business, to cease trading.

entries.clue: US agents stopping individual opening shindig? (6,5)

indicatorNotes.stopping: CIA stops up SOLE, going inside it

annotation.surface: American spies halt one person's grand opening party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a launch party; it is VENT, a hole.
annotation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party, which is one kind of gathering where people meet.

entries.clue: Horror actress best in small powerful piece (6,5)

blocks.note: the queen is the most powerful chess piece

annotation.surface: The best actress in a horror film is small but powerful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a scene or role; it is a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A film-industry nickname for a star, like Jamie Lee Curtis, known for shrieking her way through slasher movies.

entries.clue: Carve missing head of the love divinity (4)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter, so 'the' supplies T

blocks.note: to etch is to carve lines

annotation.surface: Someone carves a statue of the god of love without its head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love divinity' reads as Cupid or Eros; love is O and the definition is just 'divinity'.
annotation.definitionFit: Echo was a nymph of Greek myth, a minor divinity.

entries.clue: Period of outing cut short, like so (8)

blocks.note: sic is Latin for so, thus

annotation.surface: A day out gets cut short, just like that.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like a stretch of the outing; it is a geological period.
annotation.definitionFit: The Triassic is the geological period at the start of the dinosaur age.

entries.clue: Vehicle entering a capital city’s sports venue (9)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go inside, so QUAD goes into A ROME

annotation.surface: A vehicle drives into a capital city's stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the wordplay to 'sports venue'.
annotation.definitionFit: Formed like hippodrome from aqua, water: a lake or complex built for swimming, rowing and water-skiing.

entries.clue: Vocal praise backing lines penned by good French poet (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Vocal: LAUD as spoken sounds like LORD
indicatorNotes.backing: backing means moving in reverse, so RY becomes YR
indicatorNotes.penned by: something penned is shut in a pen, so BON encloses YR

annotation.surface: Spoken praise for a good French poet's verses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French poet' points to Verlaine or Rimbaud; 'French' belongs with 'good' and the poet is English.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Gordon, sixth Baron, wrote Don Juan and was a leading Romantic.

entries.clue: I’m unsure after complaint to worry warder (9)

indicatorNotes.after: ER comes after the other parts

blocks.note: what's eating you? = what's worrying you?

annotation.surface: A hesitant prisoner complains that the guard is fretting.
annotation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.

entries.clue: Organised armistice after removal of last blade (8)

indicatorNotes.after removal of last: ARMISTICE loses its last letter, E

annotation.surface: A truce is arranged once the last sword is put away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last blade' reads as a final weapon; 'last' is part of the deletion and 'blade' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the curved sword of the Middle East, named by its single-edged cutting steel.

entries.clue: Shot piccy with black plume, rider’s accessory (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Shot: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up

annotation.surface: A photo shows a rider with a black plume in their hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot piccy' reads as a photograph taken; 'shot' is the anagram signal. Piccy is British slang for a picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyclist carries a bicycle pump to inflate the tyres.

entries.clue: Heating devices second-class on tankers (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, B sits on top of OILERS

blocks.note: an oiler is an oil tanker

annotation.surface: Heating kit rated second-best is carried aboard the tankers.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' places B above OILERS.
annotation.definitionFit: Boilers heat water for homes and buildings.

entries.clue: An obligation to procure aluminium that’s toughened (8)

indicatorNotes.to procure: to procure is to get hold of something, so NEED takes AL in

blocks.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

annotation.surface: A duty to buy aluminium that has been hardened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Procure' looks like buying; it means taking AL in.
annotation.definitionFit: Annealed metal or glass has been heated and cooled slowly to toughen it.

entries.clue: Bug under black item of clothing (6)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, LOUSE goes under B

blocks.note: a louse is a small insect

annotation.surface: An insect lurks beneath a black garment.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' puts LOUSE below B.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a loose shirt-like top, usually worn by women, is one garment.

entries.clue: Nippy young swallows over street (6)

indicatorNotes.swallows: what is swallowed ends up inside, so FRY takes in O and ST

annotation.surface: Nimble young birds fly over a street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nippy' looks like quick and 'swallows' like birds; nippy here means chilly.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: a nippy morning is chilly enough to nip your fingers, which is how a morning with ice feels.

entries.clue: Doomed old chaps occupying ground without leader (3-6)

indicatorNotes.occupying: troops occupying ground are inside it, so O MEN sits within ILLED

annotation.surface: Elderly men occupy a field with no one in charge, and it ends badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a field; it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: Something born under bad signs or portents is fated to fail, the sense of doomed here.

entries.clue: Operated at prime locations in Dusseldorf (4)

indicatorNotes.prime locations in: take the letters at prime-numbered positions 2, 3, 5 and 7

blocks.note: the city's name, from which the letters at positions 2, 3, 5 and 7 are taken

annotation.surface: A business ran from the best sites in Düsseldorf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' reads as choice sites; it means prime-numbered letter positions, a rare device: D-U-S-S-E-L-D gives U, S, E, D.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms in the past tense: running a machine or tool, like a lathe or crane, means both.

entries.clue: Rat Queen wearing coat (8)

indicatorNotes.wearing: a wearer is inside the garment, so QU sits inside the coat SEALER

blocks.note: a sealer is a sealing coat of paint or varnish

annotation.surface: A rat and a queen both in coats.
annotation.walkthrough: A rat and a squealer are both slang for an informer.
annotation.definitionFit: A squealer, like a rat, is someone who informs on others.

entries.clue: Top award for Mark (4)

indicatorNotes.Top: to top is to cut off the head

blocks.note: an Oscar is a film award

annotation.surface: The highest prize goes to someone called Mark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top award' reads as the first prize; 'Top' is a verb meaning behead.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the trace a healed wound leaves on skin is one kind of mark.

entries.clue: Best mate losing leads in property (6)

indicatorNotes.losing leads: each word loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A best friend loses the upper hand in a property dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best mate' looks like one friend; the two words are beheaded separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a country house with its land, or everything a dead person owned, is called either.

entries.clue: Yuletide fare criticised — box with crackers (7,9)

blocks.note: to roast someone is to criticise them

annotation.surface: Christmas food gets slated, along with the box of crackers.
annotation.walkthrough: At Christmas, crackers are the paper tubes pulled at dinner; here crackers means mad, NUTS.
annotation.definitionFit: Roasted chestnuts are a traditional Christmas snack.

entries.clue: Guard small place of access (6)

blocks.note: an entry is a way in

annotation.surface: Someone keeps watch over a narrow entrance.
annotation.walkthrough: A sentry is stationed at an entry, so the pieces fit the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the soldier posted at a gate to keep watch and challenge visitors.

entries.clue: A worthy person rejected curses about big name (8)

indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is sent back, so A GEM reads backwards
indicatorNotes.about: about as in about-turn, facing the other way, so RATS reads backwards

blocks.note: a gem is a treasured person

annotation.surface: A decent person is turned away and swears about a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it reverses RATS.
annotation.definitionFit: A megastar is a very big name, a huge celebrity.

entries.clue: Day-care facility in centre of Farnham, Surrey needing refurbishment (7)

indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre letter of Farnham is N
indicatorNotes.needing refurbishment: SURREY's letters are done up in a new order

annotation.surface: A nursery in Farnham town centre, in the county of Surrey, needs doing up.
annotation.walkthrough: Farnham is a real town in Surrey, a county south-west of London, which makes the surface plausible.
annotation.definitionFit: A nursery looks after young children during the day.
